# Validation checks

[`validation.yml`](../validation.yml) reports two job checks on every pull request
and push to `main`: **Site validation** and **Exercise verification**. Use both
names as merge gates and require successful checks for the current PR revision.
There are no path filters, tolerated failures, or job conditions that skip these
checks. Pull requests use `pull_request` with a read-only contents token; checkout
credentials are not retained. The checkout and Python setup actions are pinned
to release commit SHAs.

## Site validation

- Run every `scripts/test_*.py` suite (manifest, renderer, catalog, and
  problem-layout checks), the standalone exporter suite, and CI link fixtures.
- Verify the committed manifest and HTML are current without rewriting them.
- Generate into two clean temporary directories and compare all generated bytes.
  Differences or a nonzero generator exit fail the job.
- Require exactly the 65 manifest problem pages (25/25/15) and one catalog link
  per problem. Verify each page's identity and its explicit Markdown source,
  starter when applicable, and reference links against manifest paths.
- Parse all `docs/**/*.html` files, including the shared component preview.
  Check local `href`/`src` targets, HTML fragments, duplicate IDs, CSS `url(...)`
  assets, and nonempty shared CSS/logo assets. Reject paths that leave `docs/`,
  unsupported URL schemes, and root-relative paths that would break deployment
  under the repository's GitHub Pages path.
- Validate canonical GitHub `main` resource links against local repository paths,
  including file/directory type. This avoids a network race when a PR introduces
  a new file that is not on remote `main` yet.

The validator does not fetch external websites or render JavaScript/SVG. Hosted
CDN availability, visual rendering, and accessibility remain browser QA work.

## Exercise verification

Run the existing runner's regression suite, then `scripts/verify-exercises.py`.
The runner executes 50 reference suites and 50 starter suites in separate Python
processes. All reference suites must pass. Every starter must expose a defect;
its assertion failures and the runner's exact named exception-type allowlist
are checked as teaching defects. Unexpected runtime/import errors, timeouts,
empty/skipped suites, and starters that unexpectedly pass fail the check.

The successful summary is:

```text
Solutions: 50/50 passed; starters: 50/50 exposed expected defects.
```

`PASS starter` means the runner observed an expected defect. It does not mean the
starter tests passed. No blanket acceptance of nonzero starter exits is used.

## Local replay

Use Python 3.14, matching the workflow, and run from the repository root. The
site dependencies are pinned in the existing build requirements file. Create a
virtual environment outside the checkout, then execute the same job commands:

```sh
python3.14 -m venv /tmp/bloomberg-ci-venv
. /tmp/bloomberg-ci-venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r scripts/build-site-requirements.txt
python -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
python -B scripts/export-exercise-tests.py
python -B -m unittest discover -s .github/workflows/ci -p 'test_*.py' -v
python -B .github/workflows/ci/verify_site.py
python -B scripts/verify-exercises-test.py
python -B scripts/verify-exercises.py
git diff --check
```

Any nonzero command result is a failed check and must be investigated. The CI
fixtures construct invented 65-page sites in temporary directories to demonstrate
that missing pages/catalog entries, broken targets/fragments/assets, wrong
manifest resource links, duplicate IDs, and invalid paths/schemes are rejected.
They never alter the real assignments, starters, or reference solutions.

The trigger and token choices follow GitHub's
[workflow event reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request)
and [secure use guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).
